evals.prompt: We deploy our Payload v3 + Next.js app with docker-compose (services: web on node standalone build, db postgres:18). We need a nightly job at 03:00 that finds subscriptions expiring within 7 days (collection `subscriptions`, fields `owner` relationship to users, `expiresAt` date, `notifiedAt` date) and emails each owner once. Right now nothing we queue ever executes in production, dev seems fine. Set this up end to end: the task definition, scheduling, the jobs config in payload.config.ts, and the docker-compose changes so jobs reliably run in production. Files with repo-relative paths please.
evals.expected_output: TaskConfig with schedule [{ cron, queue }]; jobs config registering the task; a runner whose queue name MATCHES the schedule queue (worker container running payload jobs:run --handle-schedules, or gated autoRun) — explaining that queued jobs need a runner in production; idempotency via notifiedAt check (email each owner once); docker-compose worker service or equivalent runnable production topology.
expectations: Task defines schedule with a 03:00 cron and an explicit queue name
A production runner exists whose queue matches the schedule queue (worker container running payload jobs:run, or gated autoRun) and the answer explains why queued jobs never ran before
Owner is emailed only once — idempotency via notifiedAt (query excludes already-notified or handler checks/sets notifiedAt)
docker-compose includes a worker service (or an explicitly justified equivalent) so jobs run reliably in production
Schedule evaluation happens exactly once across instances (--handle-schedules on the worker only / disableScheduling elsewhere)
Task handler is retry-safe: small input, re-reads fresh data inside the handler
